chunks: From him, from Safwan, from Ibn Muskān, from Abū Bakr, who said:

I asked him: A man owes me some dirhams, and he denied me and swore an oath regarding them. Is it permissible for me, if dirhams are found with him, to take from him the amount of my right? He said: Yes, but for this there is a statement (condition). I said: And what is it? He said: You say, 'O Allah, I did not take it unjustly nor treacherously, but I took it in place of my wealth which he took from me; I did not increase anything upon it.'

key_terms.بِقَدْرِ حَقِّي: To the extent of my right

ai.seo_question: How does a creditor legally recover a debt when the debtor denies it and swears an oath?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the practice of *al-kaff* (seizing assets) when a debtor denies the debt and swears an oath, a key mechanism in Shia jurisprudence for debt recovery. The Imam specifies that the creditor must recite a precise supplication affirming the seizure is merely taking back one's own property (*makana malī*) rather than an act of injustice or greed, thereby preserving the moral and legal integrity of the transaction.
